- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.4) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior 30d mean.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from 18d avg), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +3% above peak or use 20d moving average as ceiling.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.2) mid-horizon, model frequently fails to adjust downward; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per 3-day lag.
- Mean reversion is stronger in high-sentiment periods (≥0.6); if forecast deviates >+3% from 18d moving average, revert toward it with 1–2% decay per day.
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome is >+5% above 18d average, model often overreacts; apply 10–15% dampening to forecast tail (last 5 days).
- When sentiment is rising (≥0.6) and price is trending up, model tends to over-forecast; use sentiment-weighted average (e.g., 70% history, 30% sentiment) for smoothing.
